bugs.creator: kevinushey
bugs.summary: make.names() leaks its name buffer when a name is invalid in a multibyte locale

comments.text:
In a multibyte (e.g. UTF-8) locale, make.names() signals "invalid
multibyte string" for a name whose first character is valid but a later
one is not, and on every such call it leaks the buffer it had copied the
name into.

Reproducible example, in a UTF-8 locale:

    make.names("a\xff")
    ## Error in make.names("a\xff") : invalid multibyte string 1
    for (i in 1:2000) {
        try(make.names("a\xff"), silent = TRUE)
        try(make.names("1\xff"), silent = TRUE)
    }

Observed: each failing call leaks strlen(name) + 1 bytes (one more when
the name gets an "X" prefix). Expected: the error is signalled and
nothing is retained.

Analysis: do_makenames() in src/main/character.c (trunk r90590) copies
each name into an R_Calloc()ed buffer 'tmp' and frees it at the end of
the loop iteration. Only the first character is checked (by Mbrtowc)
before that copy; the mbstowcs() check that follows then signals the
error,

    if (need_prefix) {
        tmp = R_Calloc(l+2, char);
    ...
    if (mbcslocale) {
        int nc = (int) mbstowcs(NULL, tmp, 0);
        if (nc >= 0) {
            ...
        } else error(_("invalid multibyte string %lld"), (long long)i+1);

and the long jump skips the R_Free(tmp) at the end of the iteration.

Measurements: aarch64-apple-darwin25.6.0, macOS leaks after the loop
above (4000 failing calls):

    unpatched trunk r90590:  4000 leaks for 64000 total leaked bytes.
    patched:                 0 leaks for 0 total leaked bytes.

This was found with LeakSanitizer by a new fuzz target for character
functions in https://github.com/r-devel/r-oss-fuzz (a three-byte
input); the defect itself is independent of fuzzing.

Proposed patch: attached as makenames-invalid-mbcs-leak.diff. It
allocates 'tmp', and the buffer used to append "." to a reserved word,
with R_alloc() instead. The loop already resets the R_alloc stack with
vmaxset() at the end of each iteration, so on the normal path the
memory is released at the same point as before, and on the error path
the error handler releases it. The FIXME about reallocating the second
buffer goes away. Results for valid input (unique = TRUE, allow_ =
FALSE, reserved words, non-ASCII names) and the error message are
unchanged, and make test-Reg passes.

The patch is also submitted as https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/342,
where CI results can be seen.
